title: Abu Nuwas, the Three Guests and the Caliph
logline: The poet Abu Nuwas answers the caliph's mockery with a cheeky joke, is sentenced to be paraded in a donkey saddle and worse, and jokes his way from the edge of the sword to a pardon and ten thousand dirhams.
moral: Quick wit can save a man where strength and rank cannot.
tone: Light court comedy played deadpan: a merry dinner, an offended king, a clown who refuses to be humiliated. Danger is shown only as icons; the laughs come from acting.

beats.summary: A proud feast with three empty cushions.
He finds three guests in the street and invites them.
Asked to choose, he gives each a different verse: nobody loses.
The caliph mocks him with a pretend judgeship.
The poet's cheeky reply turns the mockery back on the caliph.
The caliph storms out, punishment postponed.
Next day: robe taken, donkey saddle on, parade and sword ordered.
He plays the donkey; the ladies laugh and pay him.
The deadpan line: my finest poetry for his finest clothes.
The caliph realises the poet is mocking the punishment itself.
He laughs, pardons him and pays ten thousand dirhams.
Not strength, not rank: one last joke.

props.description: Planned brass tray with food (KD-011); three variants on the table: roast dish, sweet pyramid, bread and fruit.
Planned stemmed cup 44 x 64 and matching jug (AN-099); four cups, one jug. Contents are never shown or labelled.
Planned poetry ribbon (AN-103): paper band with squiggle writing that unrolls along a curve and can carry small icons (dish, sweets, cup, moon, star, rose, crown).
The oversized white turban of the planned judge preset, drawn as a loose prop 150 wide x 90 high that can be carried, dropped on a head and pushed up.
Planned wordless picture balloon, single and strip modes; icons here: "?", scroll with "?", looping path arrow, three veiled heads, plain scimitar (also struck with a red X).
Planned folding screen (AN-090): three panels, 180 wide x 260 high, paper with blue dots and a red frame; hides the change of clothes completely.

NEW. Donkey pack saddle worn on a person: a padded hump 170 wide x 80 high sitting behind the shoulders (brown leather with red dot shading, yellow trim, two short wooden horns 30 high), a 14 wide girth strap across the chest with a buckle, and a ring at one side for the lead rope. Open top holds a coin heap (fill 0..1).
Planned coin mound and single coins (rain of 14 coins on seeded arcs in S12).
Planned small scroll with wavy lines; Jaafar's reading scroll and the pardon with a red seal.

scenes.summary: The caliph roars with laughter in spite of himself, pardons the poet before anything else can happen, has the saddle taken off and gives him ten thousand dirhams.

scenes.summary: The moral in pictures: he was saved not by strength, not by rank, but by one last joke. Wink to camera, THE END.

camera.notes: Medium on Abu alone (zoom 1.5, centre 400,660); the court soft behind. Final slow push to 1.65 by 170.4; hold for THE END.

scenes.composition: Abu at x 400 with the sack at his feet. Three icon tiles appear in a row above him at y 380 (x 250, 400, 550), 110 px each: arm, crown, speech balloon. THE END title sits in the upper third, clear of his face.

actions.action: walks forward toward the camera, sack over his shoulder, and stops

actions.action: wipes his brow; the saddle lies small on the floor behind him

actions.action: the struck-out sword icon floats up behind him and fades
actions.acting: Abu glances back at it over his shoulder and shivers once

actions.action: tile 1: a flexed arm icon; Abu tries to flex, nothing there; red X on the tile
actions.acting: aR flex pose, looks at his thin arm, shrugs

actions.action: tile 2: a small crown icon; he points at the real caliph behind and shakes his head; red X

actions.action: tile 3: a speech balloon with HA! inside; green tick, the tile pulses
actions.acting: Abu taps his own temple, then his lips: big grin

ending.description: After the last word (171.08) Abu holds his wink, the court chuckles behind him, THE END pops at 171.3 with a chime and holds to 174.9 with blinks and breathing only.

subtitles.ar: أعد أبو نواس في بيته وليمة كبيرة من اللحوم والأطعمة الفاخرة.|ثم خرج يبحث عن رفقة جميلة يشاركها الطعام والشراب والغزل.|رأى ثلاثة فتيان حسان الوجوه، فتوقف ليدعوهم إلى مجلسه.
subtitles.en: Abu Nuwas prepared a luxurious feast|and went looking for attractive company for food, wine, and flirtation.|He saw three handsome youths and invited them in.

subtitles.ar: أنشد لهم أبياتًا يمدح فيها الوليمة ومتعتها، فقبلوا الدعوة.|جلسوا يأكلون ويشربون، ثم سألوه أيهم أجمل.|اختار لكل واحد وصفًا شعريًا مختلفًا، وأبدى إعجابه بهم وقبّلهم.
subtitles.en: He recited verses praising the feast, and they accepted.|Over food and wine they asked which was most beautiful.|He praised and kissed each in turn.

subtitles.ar: اشتد به السكر، واستمر مجلس اللهو حتى سمع الجميع طرقًا على الباب.|دخل الخليفة هارون الرشيد فجأة، فنهض الحاضرون احترامًا.|سأل الخليفة أبا نواس عما يحدث في ذلك المكان.
subtitles.en: As the drinking continued, someone knocked.|Harun al-Rashid entered unexpectedly. Everyone rose respectfully,|and the caliph asked Abu Nuwas what sort of gathering this was.

subtitles.ar: سخر هارون منه وقال: لقد عينتك قاضيًا على أهل الوساطة في الفساد.|أجاب الشاعر مازحًا: وهل لديك قضية تريد عرضها علي؟|فهم الخليفة التلميح، فغضب وخرج دون أن يعاقبه فورًا.
subtitles.en: Harun mockingly appointed him judge over procurers.|Abu Nuwas quipped, “Do you have a case to bring before me?”|The caliph took offense and left angrily.

subtitles.ar: في اليوم التالي ذهب أبو نواس إلى مجلس القصر كعادته.|لكن هارون أمر الحارس مسرورًا أن ينزع عنه ثيابه، ويضع على ظهره سرج حمار،|ثم يطوف به أمام نساء القصر ويقتله.
subtitles.en: The next day Abu Nuwas attended court.|Harun ordered Masrur to strip him, dress him in donkey gear,|parade him before the palace women, and then execute him.

subtitles.ar: قاد مسرور الشاعر بين غرف النساء، منتظرًا تنفيذ بقية الأمر.|لم يكف أبو نواس عن المزاح والتمثيل، فضحكت النساء وأعطته الهدايا والنقود.|وعندما مر به جعفر البرمكي، سأله عن سبب تلك الهيئة.
subtitles.en: Masrur paraded him through the women’s chambers.|Abu Nuwas kept joking, making them laugh and earning gifts.|Jaafar the Barmecide then asked what had happened.

subtitles.ar: أجاب أبو نواس بوجه جاد:|قدمت للخليفة أفضل شعري، فأهداني أفضل ثيابه!|وصلت العبارة إلى هارون، الذي أدرك أن الشاعر يسخر حتى من العقوبة، وأنه لم يفقد سرعة بديهته.
subtitles.en: With a straight face, Abu Nuwas replied,|“I gave the caliph my finest poetry; he gave me his finest clothes.”|The joke reached Harun.

subtitles.ar: ضحك الخليفة رغم غضبه، وأمر بالعفو عن أبي نواس قبل تنفيذ الإعدام.|ثم منحه عشرة آلاف درهم.|وهكذا نجا الشاعر من عقوبة مرعبة، لا بقوته أو مكانته، بل بنكتة أخيرة.
subtitles.en: The caliph laughed despite his anger, pardoned Abu Nuwas before the execution,|and awarded him ten thousand dirhams.|One last joke saved the poet’s life.

new_assets.name: packSaddle
new_assets.description: Donkey pack saddle worn by a person, with girth strap, lead ring and an open top that fills with coins. Reusable for any punishment, porter or pack-animal gag; the same drawing can sit on the Library donkey.
new_assets.implementation: One function packSaddle(ctx, x, y, {s, fill, tilt, strap}). Hump: K rounded box 170 x 80 with brush outline, red Ben-Day dots, yellow trim line, two horn rectangles. Strap: a band drawn over the person's chest after the person (two passes: saddle behind the figure, strap in front). Anchor it to the person's shoulder point (figure-local about y -150) so it follows tip, sq and walk bob. Coins: reuse coinPile clipped to the open top.

new_assets.name: person plainShirt look
new_assets.description: A costume variant for the 'shamed' poet: ankle-length plain white long-sleeved shirt, no headwear, short hair, bare feet. Fully covered; reusable for prisoners, penitents, sleepers.
new_assets.implementation: No new drawing: person {costume:'ascetic', pal:{robe: white, dot: pale blue, shoes:'bare', hair: black, beard: black}, age: 0.2} with headwear switched off (add an opt-in headwear:false if the preset has no such switch; default unchanged for the regression test).

new_assets.name: judgeTurban (loose)
new_assets.description: The planned judge turban usable as a loose prop that can be carried and dropped on any head.
new_assets.implementation: Draw the judge preset headwear from a standalone function at (x, y, rot, s); after it lands, pass the planned headwear offset and scale 1.35 to the person so it follows the head.

new_assets.name: iconBalloon icons (path, veiled heads, scimitar, struck)
new_assets.description: Four small flat icons for the planned iconBalloon and a red X strike state. Keeps the order to execute off screen and wordless.
new_assets.implementation: Each icon is a 70 px function made of K primitives (loop arrow path; three circles with veil arcs and smile arcs; a curved blade polygon with a yellow hilt). strike 0..1 draws two red brush lines on.

owner_questions: The script calls the three 'handsome youths' and mentions flirtation: by default they are drawn as three clearly adult young gentlemen (moustaches or beards, adult size) and the scene is staged as a friendly dinner with poetry; no flirting is shown.

The script says he kissed each of them: by default this is a courtly salute from his seat (fingertips to his own lips, then a bow, hand on heart) with no contact; say if you prefer it left out completely.
Wine and drunkenness: by default plain cups and a jug with no label or visible contents, and his state is shown only as swaying, a crooked turban and three little stars.

The caliph's insult ('judge over procurers') and the poet's hint are softened in pictures to a giant mock judge turban, the lettering JUDGE?! and OF MISCHIEF, and a scroll balloon pointing at the caliph; the subtitles stay verbatim.
Stripping: by default he changes behind a folding screen and comes out fully covered in a long plain white shirt, with the donkey saddle strapped on his back; no undress is shown.
The execution order is shown only as a small scimitar icon in the caliph's balloon and Masrur's sheathed sword; the sword is never drawn and the icon is struck out at the pardon.

Invented lettering (not in the script): KNOCK! KNOCK!, THE CALIPH!, JUDGE?!, ANY CASE FOR ME?, HMPH!, HEE HAW!, HA HA HA! (twice), PARDONED!, THE END; labels ROAST, SWEETS, MASRUR, JAAFAR, DONKEY SADDLE, STRAIGHT FACE, OF MISCHIEF. Default: keep all.

Added business beyond the script: the donkey act (ear flaps, bray, hoof count), Masrur hiding a smile, the green robe being returned at the pardon, and the three tiles (arm, crown, HA!) for the moral. Default: keep.
SCRIPT: the English of P7 stops at 'The joke reached Harun.' while the Arabic adds that Harun realised the poet was mocking even the punishment and had not lost his quick wit; both are kept verbatim.
SCRIPT: the English of P8 omits the Arabic 'not by his strength or his rank' and 'a terrifying punishment', and P4 English omits 'without punishing him at once'; both are kept verbatim.
SCRIPT: the story title says 'Three Boys'; the plan title used on any card is 'Abu Nuwas, the Three Guests and the Caliph'. Default: no title card with the word boys.
implementation_notes: The narration has almost no pauses: the only gaps are 27.44 to 27.84, 129.12 to 129.64 and the tail after 171.08. Only three effects are planned (pop 27.62, tick 129.38, chime 171.3). Knocks, the door slam, the bray and the coin rain are visual only (lettering, sound arcs, shake). Do not add effects under words.
Set LIFE.t = t every frame; give every character a gaze target. Groups (three guests, three ladies) always use stagger(i) and different idles; never move in unison.
Abu has two looks. Switch poet to plainShirt while he is fully hidden by bathScreen (97.9 to 98.8) and back under the robe flourish (157.9 to 158.5). Draw order in S9/S10: hall, Abu, screen, Masrur.

packSaddle draws in two passes around the person (hump behind, strap in front) and follows tip/sq. The lead rope runs from Masrur's hand (P.hands) to the saddle ring; sag when slack, straight when taut.
Sitting at the table: person {sit: 1, seat: 'floor'} for the guests and Abu; draw the table after the seated figures behind it and before the trays, so the table hides their legs.

The caliph on the throne: person({y: HALL.throne.sitY, sit: 1, seat: 'bench'}). The house door and hall positions quoted in the plan are approximate: read them from the set anchors (MERCHANT, HALL, MARKET).
The transition card NEXT DAY... at 86.62 covers the set change from poetHouse to court: put the camera cut 0.01 s apart at the card midpoint.
Thought clouds (S2, S15) are for narrated intentions and realisation only; keep figures inside at least 110 px on screen (scale 0.3 of an s 1.2 figure, or raise the scale).
Lettering never covers a face: place KNOCK! KNOCK! on the door, HA HA HA! above the arches, HEE HAW! to the upper right of Abu, PARDONED! over the scroll.
Use panel-only shake (door slam 84.0, saddle drop 157.1). Call finish last every frame. Subtitles: Noto Naskh Arabic 700 verbatim, English below in blue Bangers; chunks as given in subtitles.
Cue times in actions are the word starts from timeline.md; anticipation starts up to 0.3 s earlier where noted. Scene S17 ends at 174.9 (audio 171.42 + 3.4 s hold).
warnings: Mature source: the story is softened in pictures (see owner_questions) while the narration and subtitles remain verbatim, including the words wine, flirtation, kissed, procurers, strip and execute. The owner should confirm this is acceptable for the channel's audience.

Depends on planned assets that are not in Library yet: person presets 'poet' and 'executioner', verseRibbon, iconBalloon, bathScreen, goblet, foodTray, purse, coinPile, scroll, flush, headwear offset, person laugh, sneak gait, rope lead, honourRobe flourish, goldGlow. If one is missing, build it in the story under the planned name.
No pauses in the narration: the film will be nearly free of sound effects; that is intended.
The person figure is front-facing only: the donkey act is played upright (ears with hands, bray, hoof tap), not on all fours.
Ten characters on four sets is a large human cast for one film; all are costume variants of one figure and no new set is needed, but staging time is high (17 scenes, about 140 keyed actions).
